claims.text: Tribological performance degrades non-linearly after ambient temperature exceeds a critical threshold.
The degradation threshold is caused by loss of protective oxide-scale integrity due to thermal-expansion mismatch.
Failure of the oxide scale shifts wear from mild oxidative wear to severe adhesive and abrasive wear driven by coating delamination.
The initial HEA coating possesses a protective oxide scale under ambient conditions.
HEA coating microstructures may contain an ordered B2 phase or complex oxides.
Thermal-expansion mismatch induces interfacial cracking in the oxide scale or at the coating-substrate interface.
Elevated-temperature phase instability, including an FCC-to-monoclinic transition, exacerbates interfacial cracking.
B2 decomposition at elevated temperature may exacerbate interfacial cracking.
At low temperatures, a stable, self-healing tribo-oxide governs wear and reduces friction.
Thermal-expansion mismatch during cooling or thermal cycling generates stresses that cause cracks in silicide coatings.
High-temperature loss of FCC structure or precipitation of brittle phases reduces coating fracture toughness.
Cracking of the oxide scale exposes metal, causing rapid oxidation and severe adhesive wear.
Oxide-scale cracking causes a sharp increase in wear rate.
The wear-rate curve will have a low, stable region followed by a sharp increase accompanied by coating delamination and spallation.
At 25 degrees Celsius, the oxide scale remains intact and wear is minimal.
The degradation boundary occurs when thermal stress exceeds the fracture resistance of the oxide-scale or coating interface.
The degradation boundary occurs below melting but after significant phase instability or acceleration of oxidation kinetics begins.
Reports on microstructural control for improving the tribological performance of refractory HEA films are scarce.
Long-term oxide-scale stability under combined thermal and mechanical stress is insufficiently documented.
Relevant phase-transition temperatures vary with alloy composition and are not characterized for all HEA systems.

contradictions.description: The stated test design lists temperatures only through 800 degrees Celsius, whereas the falsification rule requires demonstrating stable behavior across the entire range through 900 degrees Celsius.
